revision.text:
{{神社 |名称 = 気多神社 |画像 = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[兵庫県]][[豊岡市]]日高町上郷字大門227 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=気多神社}} |祭神 = [[大国主|大己貴命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
[[但馬国]][[総社]]
旧[[郷社]] |創建 = （伝）初代[[神武天皇]]9年 |本殿 = |別名 = 総社気多大明神 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[10月14日]][http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html 気多神社]（兵庫県神社庁）。 |神事 = }} [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|鳥居}}]] '''気多神社'''（けたじんじゃ）は、[[兵庫県]][[豊岡市]]日高町上郷にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]、[[但馬国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[郷社]]。 旧称は「総社気多大明神」。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の1柱境内説明板。。 * [[大国主|大己貴命]]（おおなむちのみこと） == 歴史 == 社伝では[[神武天皇]]9年に気立（気多）の丘に創建されたとするが、詳らかではない。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[但馬国]][[気多郡 (兵庫県)|気多郡]]に「気多神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列している。 [[平安時代]]頃から、各[[令制国]]の[[国府]]近くには国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]が設けられるようになるが、気多神社はそのうちの[[但馬国]]の[[総社]]とされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。[[弘安]]8年（[[1285年]]）の「但馬国大田文」に見える「惣社」に比定されるほか、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）の奉納銘を有する鰐口（気多神社蔵、豊岡市指定文化財）にも「但州気多惣社大明神」と記されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 上記の「但馬国大田文」では、惣社社領として気多郡内に大般若田4町、三十講田1町5反、毘沙門堂田5町7反、毘沙門講田1町、三昧田1町7反60歩が記載されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]3年（[[1870年]]）に社名を「気多神社」に改称し、明治6年（[[1873年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列した境内説明板。。 == 境内 == [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] 社殿は[[江戸時代]]の[[延宝]]5年（[[1677年]]）の再建と伝える。[[大正]]12年（[[1923年]]）に修理が施された。 == 摂末社 == いずれも境内社。 * 八坂神社 * 須賀神社 * 八幡神社 * 稲荷神社 * 愛宕神社 == 文化財 == === 豊岡市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf 豊岡市指定文化財一覧]}}（豊岡市ホームページ）。 ** 気多神社の鰐口 1口（工芸品） - [[室町時代]]、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）奉納銘を有する[[鰐口]]。昭和52年3月29日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=明治神社誌料編纂所編|author=|year=1912|chapter=気多神社|title=[[府県郷社明治神社誌料]]|publisher=明治神社誌料編纂所|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|明治神社誌料|1912年}}}} ** [http://kindai.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1088244/386 『明治神社誌料 府県郷社 上』]（近代デジタルライブラリーより）386コマ参照。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会編|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|中世諸国一宮制|2000年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1999|chapter=上郷村|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 29-1 兵庫県の地名 1|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490619|ref={{Harvid|上郷村（平凡社）|1999年}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[気多大社]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html 気多神社] - 兵庫県神社庁 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:けたしんしや}} [[Category:兵庫県の神社]] [[Category:豊岡市の歴史]] [[Category:但馬国の式内社]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:兵庫県の旧郷社]] [[Category:但馬国|社0]]

{{神社 |名称 = 気多神社 |画像 = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
拝殿 |所在地 = [[兵庫県]][[豊岡市]]日高町上郷字大門227 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=気多神社}} |祭神 = [[大国主|大己貴命]] |神体 = |社格 = [[式内社]]（小）
[[但馬国]][[総社]]
旧[[郷社]] |創建 = （伝）初代[[神武天皇]]9年 |本殿 = |別名 = 惣社気多大明神 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[10月14日]][http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html 気多神社]（兵庫県神社庁）。 |神事 = }} [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|鳥居}}]] '''気多神社'''（けたじんじゃ）は、[[兵庫県]][[豊岡市]]日高町上郷にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]、[[但馬国]][[総社]]で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[郷社]]。 旧称は「惣社気多大明神」。 == 祭神 == 祭神は次の1柱境内説明板。。 * [[大国主|大己貴命]]（おおなむちのみこと） == 歴史 == [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] 社伝では、国司文書において[[神武天皇]]9年に気立（気多）の丘に創建された旨の記述があるとするが、詳らかではない。『[[播磨国風土記]]』宍禾郡御方里条では、葦原志許乎命（大己貴命）と[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍命]]が黒葛を投げて国占を争ったという伝説が記され、葦原志許乎命の投げた黒葛3本のうち1本は但馬気多郡に落ちたと伝えることから、郡名を冠する当社は早くより鎮座したものと推測される{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。また社名から、[[能登国]][[一宮]]の[[気多大社]]（[[石川県]][[羽咋市]]）を始め各地の気多神社との関連が指摘される{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[但馬国]][[気多郡 (兵庫県)|気多郡]]に「気多神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列している{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 [[平安時代]]頃から、各[[令制国]]の[[国府]]近くには国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]が設けられるようになるが、気多神社はそのうちの[[但馬国]]の[[総社]]とされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。[[弘安]]8年（[[1285年]]）の「但馬国大田文」に見える「惣社」に比定されるほか、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）の奉納銘を有する鰐口（気多神社蔵、豊岡市指定文化財）にも「但州気多惣社大明神」と記されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 上記の「但馬国大田文」では、惣社社領として気多郡内に大般若田4町、三十講田1町5反、毘沙門堂田5町7反、毘沙門講田1町、三昧田1町7反60歩が記載されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]3年（[[1870年]]）に社名をそれまでの「惣社気多大明神」から「気多神社」に改称し、明治6年（[[1873年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列した境内説明板。{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 == 摂末社 == 下記の境内社5社などがある。 * 八坂神社 * 須賀神社 * 八幡神社 * 稲荷神社 * 愛宕神社 == 文化財 == === 豊岡市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf 豊岡市指定文化財一覧]}}（豊岡市ホームページ）。 ** 気多神社の鰐口 1口（工芸品） - [[室町時代]]、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）奉納銘を有する[[鰐口]]。昭和52年3月29日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=明治神社誌料編纂所編|author=|year=1912|chapter=気多神社|title=[[府県郷社明治神社誌料]]|publisher=明治神社誌料編纂所|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|明治神社誌料|1912年}}}} ** [{{NDLDC|1088244/386}} 『明治神社誌料 府県郷社 上』]（近代デジタルライブラリーより）386コマ参照。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会編|author=田畑久夫|chapter=氣多神社|year=1984|title=式内社調査報告 第19巻|publisher=[[皇學館大学]]出版部|page=|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1999|chapter=上郷村|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 29-1 兵庫県の地名 1|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490619|ref={{Harvid|上郷村（平凡社）|1999年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会編|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|中世諸国一宮制|2000年}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[気多大社]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html 気多神社] - 社伝では、国司文書において[[神武天皇]]9年に気立（気多）の丘に創建された旨の記述があるとするが、詳らかではない。『[[播磨国風土記]]』宍禾郡御方里条では、葦原志許乎命（大己貴命）と[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍命]]が黒葛を投げて国占を争ったという伝説が記され、葦原志許乎命の投げた黒葛3本のうち1本は但馬気多郡に落ちたと伝えることから、郡名を冠する当社は早くより鎮座したものと推測される{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。また社名から、[[能登国]][[一宮]]の[[気多大社]]（[[石川県]][[羽咋市]]）を始め各地の気多神社との関連が指摘される{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[但馬国]][[気多郡 (兵庫県)|気多郡]]に「気多神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列している{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 [[平安時代]]頃から、各[[令制国]]の[[国府]]近くには国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]が設けられるようになるが、気多神社はそのうちの[[但馬国]]の[[総社]]とされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。[[弘安]]8年（[[1285年]]）の「但馬国大田文」に見える「惣社」に比定されるほか、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）の奉納銘を有する鰐口（気多神社蔵、豊岡市指定文化財）にも「但州気多惣社大明神」と記されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 上記の「但馬国大田文」では、惣社社領として気多郡内に大般若田4町、三十講田1町5反、毘沙門堂田5町7反、毘沙門講田1町、三昧田1町7反60歩が記載されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]3年（[[1870年]]）に社名をそれまでの「惣社気多大明神」から「気多神社」に改称し、明治6年（[[1873年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列した境内説明板。{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 == 摂末社 == 下記の境内社5社などがある。 * 八坂神社 * 須賀神社 * 八幡神社 * 稲荷神社 * 愛宕神社 == 文化財 == [[平安時代]]頃から、各[[令制国]]の[[国府]]近くには国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]が設けられるようになるが、気多神社はそのうちの[[但馬国]]の[[総社]]とされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。[[弘安]]8年（[[1285年]]）の「但馬国大田文」に見える「惣社」に比定されるほか、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）の奉納銘を有する鰐口（気多神社蔵、豊岡市指定文化財）にも「但州気多惣社大明神」と記されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 上記の「但馬国大田文」では、惣社社領として気多郡内に大般若田4町、三十講田1町5反、毘沙門堂田5町7反、毘沙門講田1町、三昧田1町7反60歩が記載されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]3年（[[1870年]]）に社名をそれまでの「惣社気多大明神」から「気多神社」に改称し、明治6年（[[1873年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列した境内説明板。{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 == 摂末社 == 下記の境内社5社などがある。 * 八坂神社 * 須賀神社 * 八幡神社 * 稲荷神社 * 愛宕神社 == 文化財 == === 豊岡市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf 豊岡市指定文化財一覧]}}（豊岡市ホームページ）。 ** 気多神社の鰐口 1口（工芸品） - [[室町時代]]、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）奉納銘を有する[[鰐口]]。昭和52年3月29日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=明治神社誌料編纂所編|author=|year=1912|chapter=気多神社|title=[[府県郷社明治神社誌料]]|publisher=明治神社誌料編纂所|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|明治神社誌料|1912年}}}} ** [{{NDLDC|1088244/386}} 『明治神社誌料 府県郷社 上』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）386コマ参照。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会編|author=田畑久夫|chapter=氣多神社|year=1984|title=式内社調査報告 第19巻|publisher=[[皇學館大学]]出版部|page=|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}}} * {{Cite {{Shrine |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |address = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|en|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined Deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Bronze Gong** ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto Sidebar}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hyōgo Prefecture]] [[Category:Toyooka, Hyōgo]] [[Category:Tajima Province]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]]

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined Deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|Main Hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Bronze Gong** ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto Sidebar}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hyōgo Prefecture]] [[Category:Toyooka, Hyōgo]] [[Category:Tajima Province]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]]{{Sōja shrines}}[[category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]]

Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Bronze Gong** ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto Sidebar}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Hyōgo Prefecture]] [[Category:Toyooka, Hyōgo]] [[Category:Tajima Province]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]]{{Sōja shrines}}[[category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]][[Category:original pages]]

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|en|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Bronze Gong** ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * **Bronze Gong** ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Pages with redlinks to fill]][[Category:original pages]][[Category:Sōja shrines]][[Category:Pages with redlinks to {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture map~|Japan|lat_deg=36|lat_min=14|lat_sec=22.05|lon_deg=137|lon_min=11|lon_sec=52.22|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=7}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=36|lat_min=21|lat_sec=27.27|lon_deg=136|lon_min=24|lon_sec=26.05|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=7}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=36|lat_min=48|lat_sec=0.80|lon_deg=137|lon_min=2|lon_sec=39.55|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=7}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=37|lat_min=9|lat_sec=59.18|lon_deg=138|lon_min=13|lon_sec=23.41|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=7}} {{Location map~|Japan|lat_deg=35|lat_min=28|lat_sec=41.38|lon_deg=134|lon_min=47|lon_sec=35.68|mark=Red pog.svg|marksize=7}} }} [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] 社伝では、国司文書において[[神武天皇]]9年に気立（気多）の丘に創建された旨の記述があるとするが、詳らかではない。『[[播磨国風土記]]』宍禾郡御方里条では、葦原志許乎命（大己貴命）と[[アメノヒボコ|天日槍命]]が黒葛を投げて国占を争ったという伝説が記され、葦原志許乎命の投げた黒葛3本のうち1本は但馬気多郡に落ちたと伝えることから、郡名を冠する当社は早くより鎮座したものと推測される{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。また社名から、[[能登国]][[一宮]]の[[気多大社]]（[[石川県]][[羽咋市]]）を始め各地の気多神社との関連が指摘される{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[但馬国]][[気多郡 (兵庫県)|気多郡]]に「気多神社」と記載され、[[式内社]]に列している{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 [[平安時代]]頃から、各[[令制国]]の[[国府]]近くには国内の神を合祀した[[総社]]が設けられるようになるが、気多神社はそのうちの[[但馬国]]の[[総社]]とされる{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。[[弘安]]8年（[[1285年]]）の「但馬国大田文」に見える「惣社」に比定されるほか、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）の奉納銘を有する鰐口（気多神社蔵、豊岡市指定文化財）にも「但州気多惣社大明神」と記されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 上記の「但馬国大田文」では、惣社社領として気多郡内に大般若田4町、三十講田1町5反、毘沙門堂田5町7反、毘沙門講田1町、三昧田1町7反60歩が記載されている{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=409}}。 [[明治維新]]後、[[明治]]3年（[[1870年]]）に社名をそれまでの「惣社気多大明神」から「気多神社」に改称し、明治6年（[[1873年]]）に[[近代社格制度]]において[[郷社]]に列した境内説明板。{{Sfn|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}。 == 摂末社 == 下記の境内社5社などがある。 * 八坂神社 * 須賀神社 * 八幡神社 * 稲荷神社 * 愛宕神社 == 文化財 == === 豊岡市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf 豊岡市指定文化財一覧]}}（豊岡市ホームページ）。 ** 気多神社の鰐口 1口（工芸品） - [[室町時代]]、[[応永]]34年（[[1427年]]）奉納銘を有する[[鰐口]]。昭和52年3月29日指定。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist}} == 参考文献 == * 境内説明板 * {{Cite 上』]（国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション）386コマ参照。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会編|author=田畑久夫|chapter=氣多神社|year=1984|title=式内社調査報告 第19巻|publisher=[[皇學館大学]]出版部|page=|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|氣多神社（式内社）|1984年}}}} * {{Cite {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]] [[Category:Pages needing attribution 2]][[Category:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:Pages needing {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture
