{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:Completion tier 4]][[Category:tier 4]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{citation needed|Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:qq]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{citation needed|Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:Completion tier 4]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:qq]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture Shrine Association] {{Shinto}} {{citation needed|Keta Shrine}} [[Category:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:Completion tier 5]][[Category:11]][[sn:Keta Shrine (Toyooka)]][[Category:11]] {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Keta Shrine |image = [[File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Worship Hall |location = 227 Kamigō Ōmon, Hidaka-chō, Toyooka City, Hyōgo Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35|28|41.38|N|134|47|35.68|E|region:JP-28|name=Keta Shrine}} |deity = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto) |status = {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor)
Former {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}
Sōja of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} |establishment = (Tradition) Emperor Jimmu's 9th year |festivals = October 14 }} '''Keta Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|気多神社}}, ''Keta Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Toyooka, Hyōgo|en}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|en}} (minor) listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, a former {{ill|Gōsha|en}}, and the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Tajima Province|en}}. == Enshrined deity == ; Main deity * '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (Ōnamuchi no Mikoto)''' == History == According to legend, the shrine was established on the hill of Keta during the 9th year of Emperor Jimmu’s reign. However, its precise origins remain unclear.Explanatory Board in the Shrine Precincts. The {{ill|Harima no Kuni Fudoki|en}} records a myth in which Ōnamuchi no Mikoto and {{ill|Ame no Hiboko|en}} compete for dominion by throwing kudzu vines, with one of the vines landing in Keta County, linking the shrine to early regional lore.{{Harvid|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine’s name "Keta" suggests a connection to other similarly named shrines, including {{ill|Keta Taisha|en}} in {{ill|Noto Province|en}}.{{Sfn|Keta Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1984}} The shrine is listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}, compiled in 927 CE, as a minor shrine in Keta County. From the Heian period onward, it functioned as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of Tajima Province. The shrine is referenced in the {{ill|Tajima Province|en}} tax records of 1285, with landholdings across the province.{{Harvid|Medieval Provincial Shrine System|2000}} In the Meiji era, the shrine was renamed "Keta Shrine" from its historical name, "Sōja Keta Daimyōjin," and was classified as a {{ill|Gōsha|en}} under the modern shrine ranking system. == Precincts == File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) honden.JPG|main hall File:Keta-jinja (Toyooka) torii.JPG|Torii Gate === Auxiliary Shrines === The shrine grounds include five auxiliary shrines: * Yasaka Shrine * Suga Shrine * Hachiman Shrine * Inari Shrine * Atago Shrine == Cultural Properties == === Toyooka City Designated Cultural Properties === * '''Bronze Gong''' ({{ill|Wani-guchi|en}}) - An artifact from the Muromachi period, bearing a 1427 CE inscription.{{PDFlink|[http://www.city.toyooka.lg.jp/www/contents/1152009907468/files/pdf5.pdf Toyooka City Cultural Property List]}} Designated on March 29, 1977. == Access == * 20-minute drive from {{ill|Toyooka Station|en}} on the JR San'in Main Line. == External Links == {{Commonscat|Keta-jinja (Toyooka)}} * [http://www.hyogo-jinjacho.com/data/6322192.html Keta Shrine - Hyōgo Prefecture
